project.name: Warp — input/editing/keybinding stack
project.description: Scoped analysis of three Rust crates forming Warp's input/editing/keybinding stack: warpui_core (bespoke in-house UI framework + the keymap/keybinding engine), editor (rich-text editing engine), and vim (modal-editing library). Built to support work on a more configurable keybinding engine, a better keybinding settings UI, and pluggable modal editing modes (vim/helix/kakoune).

nodes.name: draw_text
nodes.summary: Draws a text frame at a content position, applying an optional paint-style override and the base style.

nodes.name: RenderableParagraph

nodes.name: BlockPlaceholder
nodes.summary: Draws hint/placeholder text for empty blocks, tracking a layout state machine to decide when and where to show it.

nodes.name: RenderableRunnableCommand
nodes.summary: Renderable block for a runnable-command block, painting a run footer and border and dispatching click-to-run events.

nodes.name: paint

nodes.name: RenderableTable
nodes.summary: Renderable block for markdown tables, owning viewport bounds and a horizontal scrollbar and handling paint plus pointer events.

nodes.name: TableLayoutReport
nodes.summary: Geometry snapshot of a laid-out table (column widths/lefts, row heights/tops, header height, total height) used for hit-testing and painting.

nodes.name: paint_selection

nodes.summary: RenderableBlock implementation for a task-list (checkbox) line, holding the checkbox icon, sizing, and placeholder content.

nodes.summary: Constructs a RenderableTaskList from completion state, styles, viewport item and mouse state, assembling the checkbox icon and click target.

nodes.name: temporary_block.rs
nodes.summary: Renderable element for transient overlay blocks (e.g. inline decorations shown during edits) layered over the normal content.

nodes.name: RenderableTemporaryBlock
nodes.summary: RenderableBlock implementation wrapping a viewport item with an overlay decoration and text decoration for temporary on-screen blocks.

nodes.summary: Paints the temporary block's decoration and decorated text overlay into the render context.

nodes.name: text_block.rs
nodes.summary: Minimal renderable element wrapping a viewport item to paint a plain text block.

nodes.name: RenderableTextBlock
nodes.summary: RenderableBlock implementation for a plain paragraph/text block, delegating layout to its viewport item.

nodes.name: unordered_list.rs

nodes.name: RenderableBulletList
nodes.summary: RenderableBlock implementation for a bullet list item, holding the bullet glyph, its size, and the placeholder content.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Builds a RenderableBulletList for a given indent level, selecting the bullet glyph and computing its placement from styles.

nodes.name: paint
nodes.summary: Paints the bullet glyph and the list item content into the render context.

nodes.name: layout.rs
nodes.summary: Text layout engine: turns text and rich-text styles into laid-out text frames, resolving fonts, paragraph styles, style runs, and converting markdown inline nodes into styled text.

nodes.name: TextLayout
nodes.summary: Layout helper bundling the layout cache, font cache, rich-text styles and max width used to lay out paragraphs and placeholders.

nodes.name: style_and_font
nodes.summary: Resolves a paragraph's effective font and style attributes by merging paragraph styles with rich-text style overrides.

nodes.name: markdown_inline_to_text_and_style_runs
nodes.summary: Flattens a markdown inline tree into plain text plus the per-range style runs (links, inline code, emphasis) needed to lay it out.

nodes.name: layout_text_with_options
nodes.summary: Lays out a string into a text frame with explicit max width and alignment options, applying the given style runs.

nodes.name: layout_placeholder
nodes.summary: Lays out placeholder text for an empty block of a given type.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Barrel module for the editor render layer, re-exporting the element, layout and model submodules.

nodes.name: mod_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Integration-style tests for the rendering pipeline, driving edits and markdown through a TestState harness and asserting rendered output and buffer contents.

nodes.name: TestState
nodes.summary: Test harness bundling editor content, selection and render state with helpers to apply edits/selections and assert rendered output.

nodes.name: bounds.rs
nodes.summary: Geometry helpers that compute a block's content, visible, and reserved boxes/origins from a y-offset and block spacing.

nodes.name: visible_box
nodes.summary: Computes the visible bounding box of a block given its y-offset, content size and spacing.

nodes.name: reserved_box
nodes.summary: Computes the reserved bounding box (including margins) of a block from its y-offset, content size and spacing.

nodes.name: debug.rs
nodes.summary: Debug-description utilities: a Describe trait and Description type used to produce human-readable dumps of the render model tree.

nodes.name: Describe
nodes.summary: Trait for types that can write a structured human-readable description of themselves for debugging the render tree.

nodes.name: describe_to
nodes.summary: Writes a structured debug description of a render-model value into the formatter.

nodes.name: location.rs
nodes.summary: Hit-testing for the render model: defines the Location enum (block vs text position) and converts render/viewport x,y coordinates into a concrete document location.

nodes.name: Location
nodes.summary: Enum describing a hit-tested position as either a Block location or a Text offset within the rendered document.

nodes.name: coordinates_to_location
nodes.summary: Core hit-test: resolves an (x, y) render coordinate to a Location by walking blocks and paragraphs, honoring hit-test options.

nodes.name: render_coordinates_to_location
nodes.summary: Public hit-test entry converting render-space coordinates into a Location.

nodes.name: location_in_paragraph_block
nodes.summary: Resolves the text location within a paragraph block for a given coordinate.

nodes.name: location_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for coordinate-to-location hit-testing across tables, lists, code blocks, soft-wrapped lines, scrolling, and mermaid blocks.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Core render model of the editor: the central RenderState plus the laid-out block/paragraph/table types, rich-text styles, selections, decorations, viewport char ranges, autoscroll and layout-action handling.
nodes.languageNotes: Very large module (~4800 lines) aggregating the entire render-side data model; RenderState is the central stateful struct with ~90 methods.

nodes.name: RenderState
nodes.summary: Central render-side state for an editor view: owns content, selections, decorations, viewport, styles and pending edits, and drives layout, scrolling, autoscroll and hit-testing.

nodes.name: RichTextStyles
nodes.summary: Aggregate style configuration for rendered rich text: fonts, colors, code/table/checkbox/horizontal-rule styling and block spacings.

nodes.name: BlockItem
nodes.summary: Enum of all renderable block kinds (paragraph, header, code block, table, task/unordered/ordered list, image, mermaid, horizontal rule, embedded, hidden, trailing newline).

nodes.name: Paragraph
nodes.summary: A laid-out paragraph: its text frame, offset map, sizing, detected URL and spacing, with helpers for character bounds and soft-wrap conversion.

nodes.name: ParagraphBlock
nodes.summary: A block composed of one or more laid-out paragraphs, exposing combined sizing and line access.

nodes.name: LaidOutTable
nodes.summary: A fully laid-out markdown table with per-cell layouts, row/column geometry, horizontal scrolling state and hit-testing/offset mapping.

nodes.name: CellLayout
nodes.summary: Per-cell layout within a table: line heights, y-offsets, char ranges, widths and caret positions, with line/char hit-testing helpers.

nodes.name: SoftWrapPoint
nodes.summary: A (row, column) position within a soft-wrapped paragraph, with navigation between wrapped rows.

nodes.name: RenderedSelection
nodes.summary: A rendered selection range (head/tail plus cursor bias) used to draw cursors and highlights.

nodes.name: RenderedSelectionSet
nodes.summary: Ordered collection of rendered selections supporting iteration, sorting and mapping.

nodes.name: HiddenBlockConfig
nodes.summary: Configuration for a collapsed/hidden block region, tracking line count, content length and expansion gutter buttons.

nodes.name: Decoration
nodes.summary: A text decoration range (background fill and/or dashed underline) applied during rendering.

nodes.name: LayoutAction
nodes.summary: Enum of layout-mutating actions (selection/decoration change, buffer edit, temporary block, autoscroll, scroll-to) processed by RenderState.

nodes.name: AutoScrollMode
nodes.summary: Enum of autoscroll strategies (into-viewport, exact-vertical, to-selections, center-offset).

nodes.name: handle_layout_action
nodes.summary: Dispatches a LayoutAction against RenderState, applying selection/decoration/edit/scroll changes and scheduling relayout.

nodes.name: layout_pending_edit
nodes.summary: Re-lays out the portion of the document affected by a pending edit, splicing new block items into the existing layout.

nodes.name: autoscroll
nodes.summary: Adjusts the viewport scroll offsets to satisfy a requested AutoScrollMode (reveal offsets, center, follow selections).

nodes.name: blocks_in_line_range
nodes.summary: Returns the laid-out block items intersecting a given line range, used for incremental rendering.

nodes.name: dedupe_hidden_ranges
nodes.summary: Merges adjacent/overlapping hidden line ranges so collapsed regions render as single blocks.

nodes.name: multiselect_autoscroll_bounding_box
nodes.summary: Computes the bounding box covering all selection heads to drive autoscroll for multiple cursors.

nodes.name: set_viewport_size
nodes.summary: Updates the viewport size on RenderState and triggers any layout needed for the new dimensions.

nodes.name: draw_selection
nodes.summary: Draws the active selection (cursors and highlight ranges) for a render model into the context.

nodes.name: draw_cursor
nodes.summary: Draws a single cursor at a character offset with the configured cursor styling and bias.

nodes.name: draw_charwise_highlight
nodes.summary: Draws a character-wise selection highlight spanning a start/end offset across possibly soft-wrapped lines.

nodes.name: mod_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the render model: sizing, soft-wrap points, character bounds, ordered-list counting, autoscroll bounding boxes, hidden-range deduping, and table cell/offset hit-testing.

nodes.name: offset_map.rs
nodes.summary: OffsetMap mapping between content (document) offsets and frame (rendered) offsets via selectable text runs, accounting for placeholders.

nodes.name: OffsetMap
nodes.summary: Maps content offsets to frame offsets (and back) through a list of selectable text runs.

nodes.name: translate
nodes.summary: Translates an offset across the run list, handling placeholder/non-selectable runs between content and frame coordinates.

nodes.name: offset_map_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for OffsetMap content/frame translation including placeholder runs and an end-to-end mapping scenario.

nodes.name: positioned.rs
nodes.summary: Positioned<T> wrapper that assigns a start char offset, line and y-offset (plus style) to each block item, with constructors for every block kind and bounds helpers.

nodes.name: Positioned
nodes.summary: Generic wrapper attaching start char-offset, line, y-offset and style to a laid-out block item, exposing content/visible/reserved origins.

nodes.name: saved_positions.rs
nodes.summary: Generates stable per-model identifiers for the cursor, text selection and hovered block-start positions.

nodes.name: SavedPositions
nodes.summary: Holds a model id and derives stable IDs for cursor, text-selection and hovered-block positions.

nodes.name: table_offset_map.rs
nodes.summary: Offset mapping for markdown tables: maps linear offsets to cell/row/column positions and converts between source markdown offsets and rendered cell offsets.

nodes.name: TableOffsetMap
nodes.summary: Maps a linear character offset within a table to its cell/row/column and back, tracking cell ranges and separator positions.

nodes.name: TableCellOffsetMap
nodes.summary: Maps between a table cell's rendered offsets and its source markdown offsets via fragment ranges.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Builds a TableOffsetMap from per-cell lengths, computing cumulative cell and row ranges and the row/col index.

nodes.name: position_at_offset
nodes.summary: Resolves a linear table offset to a TablePosition (in-cell, on-tab separator, or on-newline).

nodes.name: from_inline_and_source
nodes.summary: Builds a TableCellOffsetMap by aligning a cell's rendered inline content with its source markdown fragments.

nodes.name: test_utils.rs
nodes.summary: Test helpers for the render model: build mock and real laid-out paragraphs, unordered lists and tables from text and styles, plus logging init.

nodes.name: layout
nodes.summary: Lays out text into render-model paragraphs/blocks for use in tests, mirroring the production layout path.

nodes.name: viewport.rs
nodes.summary: Viewport state and iteration: tracks scroll position and size, clamps and autoscrolls scroll offsets, computes viewport sizing, and iterates the block items currently visible.

nodes.name: ViewportState
nodes.summary: Holds viewport width/height and scroll top/left, with scrolling, clamping, autoscroll and sizing operations.

nodes.name: ViewportItem
nodes.summary: A block item positioned within the viewport, exposing content/visible/reserved bounds and its block offset.

nodes.name: ScrollPositionSnapshot
nodes.summary: Captures a scroll position as a stable first-visible character offset so it survives relayout.

nodes.name: ViewportIterator
nodes.summary: Iterator yielding the block viewport items intersecting the current scroll window.

nodes.name: autoscroll
nodes.summary: Adjusts scroll top/left so a target item range becomes visible, optionally scrolling horizontally.

nodes.name: viewport_size
nodes.summary: Computes the viewport size from layout constraints, size buffer and max width.

nodes.name: viewport_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for viewport offset math, item-to-block mapping, scroll bounds, and width/height change handling.

nodes.name: search.rs
nodes.summary: In-editor search: the Searcher drives literal/regex/case-sensitive find over the buffer, navigates between matches, restores selection across edits, and produces result decorations.

nodes.name: Searcher
nodes.summary: Owns search query/options and results over a buffer+selection model, with async search, match navigation, and decoration output.

nodes.name: run_search
nodes.summary: Builds the query and runs an async search over the buffer, updating the stored results.

nodes.name: restore_selected_result
nodes.summary: Re-selects the closest valid match after the buffer changes so search selection survives edits.

nodes.name: select_previous_result
nodes.summary: Moves the selected match to the previous result, wrapping around the result list.

nodes.name: result_decorations
nodes.summary: Builds the highlight decorations for all search matches plus the active match.

nodes.name: search_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for literal search, match navigation, and search-result validity across edits.

nodes.name: selection.rs
nodes.summary: Selection engine: the SelectionModel manages cursors and selections, normalizes and validates select actions, and navigates by character/word/line/paragraph including multiselect and skipping rendered mermaid blocks.

nodes.name: SelectionModel
nodes.summary: Owns cursors/selections over render+content+selection models, normalizing actions and navigating by character/word/line/paragraph with hidden-line and mermaid awareness.

nodes.name: TextUnit
nodes.summary: Enum of navigation granularities (character, word, line boundary, line, paragraph boundary).

nodes.name: SelectionMode
nodes.summary: Enum of selection modes (character, word, line) for drag/extend selection.

nodes.name: begin_selection
nodes.summary: Begins a selection at an offset in the given mode, optionally clearing existing selections (drag start).

nodes.name: normalized_character_action
nodes.summary: Normalizes a character select action by adjusting offsets around rendered mermaid blocks and clamping to valid bounds.

nodes.name: update_selections_internal
nodes.summary: Applies a selection update, recomputing goal columns and pushing the new selection set into the render model.

nodes.name: navigate_line
nodes.summary: Moves a cursor vertically by line, preserving the goal x-column across soft-wrapped and varied-height lines.

nodes.name: navigate_word
nodes.summary: Moves a cursor by word according to the word policy and direction.

nodes.name: navigate_line_boundary
nodes.summary: Moves a cursor to the start/end line boundary, accounting for indentation and soft wrapping.

nodes.name: validate_select_action
nodes.summary: Validates and clamps a select action against the current document bounds before applying it.

nodes.name: selection_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Tests for selection movement and navigation: goal-column behavior, word/line/paragraph boundaries, multiselect vertical movement, mermaid-block skipping, and semantic drag selection.

nodes.name: find_char.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Vim's f/F/t/T on-line character search, scanning a line forward or backward from the cursor column to the Nth occurrence of a target character and returning the destination column.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the `vim` modal-editing library; declares the submodules and re-exports the public motion, text-object, register, word-iterator, and FSA APIs.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust crate root (lib.rs) acting as a barrel of `mod`/`pub use` re-exports.

nodes.name: matching_brackets.rs
nodes.summary: Finds the matching bracket for a bracket character at a given buffer offset by scanning in the appropriate direction and tracking nesting depth.

nodes.name: paragraph_iterator.rs
nodes.summary: Buffer scanning helpers that locate the previous paragraph start and next paragraph end (blank-line boundaries) from an offset, used by paragraph motions and text objects.

nodes.name: register.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the black-hole register constant and a predicate validating Vim register names.

nodes.name: block.rs
nodes.summary: Computes Vim `ib`/`ab` block text objects (inside/around bracket pairs), expanding from the cursor to the enclosing brackets and adjusting for surrounding whitespace.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Barrel module aggregating the Vim text-object implementations (word, paragraph, quote, block) and re-exporting their public functions.

nodes.name: paragraph.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Vim `ip`/`ap` paragraph text objects, computing inner and around paragraph ranges including handling of surrounding blank lines.

nodes.name: quote.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Vim `i"`/`a"` quote text objects, locating the enclosing quote pair on the current line and returning the inner or around character range.

nodes.name: quote_tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the quote text-object functions, asserting inner and around quote range computation across many cursor positions and quote layouts.

nodes.name: word.rs
nodes.summary: Implements Vim `iw`/`aw` word text objects, expanding from the cursor over a run of like-kind characters and (for `aw`) trailing or leading whitespace.

nodes.summary: Core of the Vim modal-editing engine: defines the mode/motion/operator/event-type vocabulary, the `VimFSA` keystroke state machine, and the `VimModel`/`VimHandler` that translate keystrokes into concrete editor events.

nodes.summary: Vim-semantics word iterator: classifies characters into word/symbol/whitespace kinds and yields word-head and word-tail offsets forward or backward through a text buffer for w/b/e/ge style motions.

nodes.name: vim_find_char_on_line
nodes.summary: Scans a line forward or backward from the current column for the Nth occurrence of a target character, returning the destination column adjusted for at-char vs before-char (t/T) semantics and selection handling.

nodes.name: vim_find_matching_bracket
nodes.summary: Given a bracket character at an offset, scans the buffer in the matching direction while tracking nesting depth to return the offset of the complementary bracket.

nodes.name: find_previous_paragraph_start
nodes.summary: Scans backward from an offset over non-blank lines to find the start offset of the previous paragraph (the preceding blank-line boundary).

nodes.name: find_next_paragraph_end
nodes.summary: Scans forward from an offset to find the end offset of the next paragraph (the following blank-line boundary).

nodes.name: valid_register_name
nodes.summary: Predicate returning whether a character is a usable Vim register name (alphanumeric or the black-hole register).

nodes.name: vim_inner_block
nodes.summary: Computes the inner-block (`ib`) range by delegating to `vim_a_block` and trimming the surrounding brackets and optional padding whitespace.

nodes.name: vim_a_block
nodes.summary: Computes the around-block (`ab`) range by identifying the bracket under or enclosing the cursor and locating its matching partner.

nodes.summary: Computes the inner-paragraph (`ip`) range, treating either a run of blank lines or a run of content as the object bounded by paragraph boundaries.

nodes.name: vim_a_paragraph
nodes.summary: Computes the around-paragraph (`ap`) range, extending the inner paragraph to include adjacent blank lines per Vim semantics.

nodes.name: vim_inner_quote
nodes.summary: Computes the inner-quote (`i"`) range by narrowing the around-quote range to exclude the surrounding quote characters.

nodes.name: vim_a_quote
nodes.summary: Computes the around-quote (`a"`) range by locating the enclosing pair of quote characters on the current line relative to the cursor.

nodes.name: vim_inner_word
nodes.summary: Computes the inner-word (`iw`) range by expanding over the contiguous run of same-kind (word/symbol/whitespace) characters around the cursor.

nodes.name: vim_a_word
nodes.summary: Computes the around-word (`aw`) range, expanding over the word under the cursor plus trailing (or leading) whitespace per Vim rules.

nodes.name: test_a_quote
nodes.summary: Table-driven test asserting `vim_a_quote` returns the correct around-quote ranges for varied cursor positions and quote layouts.

nodes.name: test_inner_quote
nodes.summary: Table-driven test asserting `vim_inner_quote` returns the correct inner-quote ranges across cursor positions.

nodes.name: vim_word_iterator_from_offset
nodes.summary: Factory that builds a boxed word-head or word-tail iterator from a buffer offset, direction, bound, and word type for Vim w/b/e/ge motions.

nodes.summary: Classifies a character as word-char, symbol, or whitespace and exposes word-boundary equivalence used to delimit Vim words.

nodes.name: WordHeadsVim
nodes.summary: Iterator yielding offsets of word starts (heads) by stepping through the buffer and detecting character-kind transitions per Vim semantics.

nodes.name: WordTailsVim
nodes.summary: Iterator yielding offsets of word ends (tails) by stepping through the buffer and detecting character-kind transitions per Vim semantics.

nodes.name: VimMotion
nodes.summary: Enumerates all cursor motions (character, word, line, find-char, paragraph, bracket jumps, line jumps) the engine can emit.

nodes.name: VimEventType
nodes.summary: The full vocabulary of high-level editor events the Vim engine emits (insert, navigate, operation, search, visual, paste, undo, scroll, LSP actions), with dot-repeat filtering.

nodes.name: VimOperator
nodes.summary: Vim operators (delete, change, yank, case toggles, comment toggle) applied to a motion or text object.

nodes.name: PendingAction
nodes.summary: Represents a partially-entered command awaiting more input (operator, g/z prefixes, find-char, bracket, set-register).

nodes.name: TextObjectType
nodes.summary: The kinds of Vim text objects (word, paragraph, quote, block) selectable with i/a operators.

nodes.name: QuoteType
nodes.summary: Quote variants (single, double, backtick) for quote text objects, with a char-matching predicate.

nodes.name: BracketType
nodes.summary: Bracket pair kinds (parenthesis, curly brace, square bracket) for block text objects and bracket jumps.

nodes.name: BracketChar
nodes.summary: A bracket character decomposed into its end (opening/closing) and kind, with predicates for char matching and complement lookup.

nodes.name: WordType
nodes.summary: Distinguishes default words from WORDs (big words), controlling how character kinds delimit a word.

nodes.name: VimModel
nodes.summary: Public facade wrapping a VimFSA that exposes typed-character, keypress, mode, force-insert, and interrupt operations and emits events through a context.

nodes.name: VimHandler
nodes.summary: Effect handler that maps each VimEventType to a concrete editor operation (insert, navigate, operate, search, visual, paste, LSP, scroll).

nodes.name: VimSubscriber
nodes.summary: Subscriber that receives VimEvents and dispatches them to the VimHandler operations.

nodes.name: VimState
nodes.summary: Lightweight snapshot of the current Vim mode and pending showcmd string for UI display.

nodes.name: for_dot_repeat
nodes.summary: Maps a VimEventType to the event (if any) that should be recorded for the `.` dot-repeat command.

nodes.name: compute_event_count

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Cross-platform async facade for warpui_core: selects the native or wasm executor implementation via cfg, re-exports the executor/spawning API, and defines core async primitives like FutureId, SpawnedFutureHandle, and the FutureExt::with_timeout extension.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cfg_if to swap between `native` and `wasm` submodules behind a shared `imp` alias; a blanket `impl<F: Future> FutureExt for F` adds `with_timeout` to every future.

nodes.name: executor.rs
nodes.summary: Native executor implementation providing the Foreground main-thread executor and a multi-threaded tokio-backed Background runtime, with abortable task spawning and tracing span instrumentation.
nodes.languageNotes: Foreground runs tasks on the main thread via async_task::spawn_local with a custom schedule that re-dispatches through the platform delegate; Background wraps a tokio multi-thread runtime built with a custom worker count and thread-name function.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Native async module root: re-exports async_io's block_on/Timer and the executor submodule, and defines the Send-bounded Spawnable/Stream/SpawnableOutput/TransportStream trait aliases required by the multi-threaded runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `trait_set!` to declare trait aliases; native variants require `Send` bounds for the multi-threaded tokio executor.

nodes.name: executor.rs
nodes.summary: WASM executor implementation where all tasks are local (no background threads): provides Foreground and Background executors backed by wasm_bindgen_futures spawn_local, with abortable spawning.
nodes.languageNotes: On wasm every future runs on the single main thread, so Background simply delegates to local spawning and tasks are non-Send.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: WASM async module root: re-exports block_on and a gloo-timers-backed Timer that mirrors async_io::Timer, and defines relaxed (non-Send) trait aliases for spawnable tasks/streams on the single-threaded wasm runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: Provides a custom Timer wrapping gloo TimeoutFuture and implementing both Future and Stream; trait aliases drop the Send bound since wasm is single-threaded.

nodes.name: FutureId
nodes.summary: Copyable newtype wrapping a monotonically increasing usize that uniquely identifies a spawned future; used in tests to await specific spawned futures.

nodes.name: SpawnedFutureHandle
nodes.summary: Handle returned when spawning a future on an executor; exposes abort() to cancel the task and future_id() to await it in tests.

nodes.name: SpawnedLocalStream
nodes.summary: Wrapper around a LocalBoxFuture representing a spawned local stream, primarily used in tests to extract the underlying future.

nodes.name: FutureExt
nodes.summary: Extension trait, blanket-implemented for all Futures, adding with_timeout() which races the future against a Timer and yields a TimeoutError if the duration elapses.

nodes.name: BackgroundTask
nodes.summary: Abortable handle to a task running on the Background tokio runtime; implements Future (via poll) so callers can await its result, plus abort()/detach() to control its lifecycle.

nodes.name: Foreground
nodes.summary: Main-thread executor (Platform or Test variant) that spawns local futures via async_task and reschedules them onto the main thread through the platform delegate; errors if constructed off the main thread.

nodes.name: Background
nodes.summary: Multi-threaded background executor wrapping a tokio runtime built with a custom worker count and thread-name function; spawns Send futures and supports abortable tasks.

nodes.name: Foreground
nodes.summary: WASM main-thread executor that spawns local (non-Send) futures via wasm_bindgen_futures spawn_local; on wasm everything runs on the single thread.

nodes.name: Background
nodes.summary: WASM 'background' executor that, since wasm has no real threads, also spawns local futures via spawn_local; mirrors the native Background API with abortable spawning.

nodes.name: Timer
nodes.summary: Drop-in replacement for async_io::Timer on wasm, backed by gloo TimeoutFuture; implements both Future and Stream and supports after/at/never constructors.

tour.title: Orientation: Three Crates
tour.description: Start here to see the shape of the whole stack. warpui_core is Warp's bespoke, GPUI-like UI framework and keymap engine; the editor crate is a rich-text editing engine; and the vim crate is a standalone modal-editing library. The three Cargo manifests encode the dependency direction that drives this entire tour: the vim manifest depends on warp_core and warpui_core, and the editor manifest builds on the same UI runtime, so both higher-level crates point down at warpui_core rather than the other way around.

tour.title: Crate Entry Points
tour.description: Each crate's lib.rs is its public front door, declaring submodules and re-exporting the types that the rest of the workspace consumes. warpui_core/src/lib.rs wires up actions, elements, keymap, platform, and rendering; editor/src/lib.rs exposes the content, render, and selection layers; and vim/src/lib.rs surfaces the motion, text-object, and FSA APIs. Reading these three roots side by side gives you the table of contents for everything that follows.
tour.languageLesson: In Rust a crate root (lib.rs) uses `mod` to declare submodules and `pub use` to re-export their items, building a curated public API surface. A `mod foo;` declaration is structural ownership (the file is part of this crate), which is distinct from a `use` import that merely references another module's items.

tour.title: The Framework Runtime
tour.description: This is the reactive substrate everything else dispatches through. AppContext in core/app.rs owns all models, views, windows, ref-counts, and executors, while core/mod.rs defines the foundational Handle, Effect, and Subscription types and the model/view submodules supply the entity-and-handle reactivity. The presenter then drives the per-frame lifecycle, building a Scene from the view tree and dispatching events and actions into it. Every keystroke, edit, and repaint you will trace later flows through this loop.
tour.languageLesson: WarpUI uses the entity/handle pattern: state lives in a central AppContext arena and code holds lightweight, ref-counted Handles rather than owning the data directly. This sidesteps Rust's borrow-checker friction for graph-shaped UI state while keeping mutation centralized and observable.

tour.title: Input Events & Actions
tour.description: Before keybindings can mean anything, the framework needs a vocabulary of raw input and dispatchable intent. event.rs defines the Event enum (key, mouse, scroll, drag, IME) plus modifier and key state, while actions.rs declares the StandardAction set of OS-level commands and core/action.rs provides the dynamic, downcastable Action trait. The keymap engine in the next steps exists precisely to translate Events from this layer into Actions that the presenter from Step 3 dispatches.

tour.title: The Keymap Engine: Bindings
tour.description: This is the spine of the tour. keymap.rs defines the core keybinding model: keystrokes, the distinction between fixed (built-in) and editable (user-customizable) bindings, triggers, binding descriptions, and the Keymap registry used to look up and override bindings. Understanding the fixed-versus-editable split here is the foundation for any work on a more configurable engine or a better keybinding settings UI, since editable bindings are exactly what a settings surface would mutate.
tour.languageLesson: The fixed-vs-editable binding split is a deliberate configurability seam: fixed bindings ship with the app and cannot be overridden, while editable bindings layer user customization on top. A configurable keybinding engine grows by widening the editable set and giving it a stable serialization format that a settings UI can read and write.

tour.title: Context Predicates & the Matcher
tour.description: Bindings only fire in the right situation, and this is where that decision is made. keymap/context.rs defines the Context (active flags plus a key/value map) and the ContextPredicate boolean expression tree, with operator overloads and macros forming a small predicate DSL for when a binding applies. keymap/matcher.rs is the state machine that registers bindings, resolves pending multi-key sequences, validates bindings per context, and maps keystrokes to standard or custom actions. This matcher is the single most important file for the project's goal of pluggable modal modes — vim, helix, or kakoune layers ultimately register and resolve through here.
tour.languageLesson: The matcher is a keystroke state machine: a multi-key chord like `g d` leaves the matcher in a pending state after the first key, waiting to either complete a binding or time out and replay the buffered keys. Context predicates gate which bindings are even eligible, so the same keystroke can resolve to different actions depending on focus and mode — the exact mechanism a pluggable modal scheme rides on.

tour.title: Text Primitives & Layout
tour.description: With input handled, we turn to the text it operates on. text/mod.rs defines the TextBuffer trait that abstracts char/point/offset navigation and selection classification, the shared vocabulary used across both the UI framework and the editor. text_layout.rs is the shaping and layout engine that turns styled content into laid-out Lines and TextFrames with glyph runs, caret positioning, and clipping, backed by a content-and-style-keyed LayoutCache. Together they are the bridge between abstract document positions and pixels on screen.

tour.title: The Input UI Surface
tour.description: Now we see where input and text become a visible widget. elements/mod.rs defines the foundational Element and ParentElement traits plus geometry primitives that every concrete element composes from, ui_components/text_input.rs wraps the editor element as a styled single- or multi-line input, and ui_components/keyboard_shortcut.rs renders key chords as platform-appropriate key caps. The keyboard_shortcut component is the visual counterpart to the keymap engine from Steps 5-6 — it is how a settings UI would display the very bindings the matcher resolves.

tour.title: The Editor Content Model
tour.description: Crossing into the editor crate, this is the data model that holds and mutates document state. content/buffer.rs is the central rich-text buffer engine, owning a sum-tree text store, selections, undo, and styling and emitting BufferEvents; content/text.rs is the underlying BufferText sum-tree of styled block items. selection_model.rs maps anchor-backed selections to and from buffer offsets and merges overlaps, while undo.rs groups edits into reversible, time-bounded atomic steps. These are the structures that vim motions and operators will eventually drive.
tour.languageLesson: The buffer is backed by a sum-tree (a balanced B-tree over text with cached summaries), which makes positional queries and edits logarithmic rather than linear over a large document. Summaries let the editor answer questions like "what offset is this line/point at?" without scanning the whole buffer.

tour.title: Anchors & the Editor Model
tour.description: Building on the buffer from Step 9, this step covers how positions stay stable and how editing behavior specializes. content/anchor.rs defines text anchors that track stable positions across edits via a sum-tree, with an Anchors registry keeping live handles in sync as the buffer mutates — the mechanism that keeps cursors and selections correct after an insert or delete. editor/model.rs layers CoreEditorModel over the buffer to drive edits, selections, and cursor movement, with PlainTextEditorModel and RichTextEditorModel specializing plain versus markdown editing. multiline.rs keeps CR/LF/CRLF handling correct across all of it.

tour.title: Editor Rendering
tour.description: This is how the content model becomes painted output through warpui_core. render/model/mod.rs holds the central RenderState plus the laid-out block, paragraph, and table types, rich-text styles, viewport ranges, and autoscroll handling; render/layout.rs resolves fonts and style runs into laid-out text frames; and render/element/mod.rs is the rich-text rendering element that owns the block layout/paint pipeline, hit-testing, mouse/keyboard dispatch, and cursor blink. editor.rs ties these into the public EditorView surface. This cluster is the most tightly coupled subsystem in the editor and is best read together.

tour.title: The Vim Modal Engine
tour.description: Now we reach how a modal scheme layers on top of everything below it. vim/src/vim.rs is the core of the engine: it defines the mode, motion, operator, and event-type vocabulary, the VimFSA keystroke state machine, and the VimModel/VimHandler that translate keystrokes into concrete editor events. Crucially, vim does not own the buffer — it consumes the editor's content model from Steps 9-10 and emits editor events, while its keystrokes ultimately enter through the keymap matcher from Step 6. This separation is exactly the seam where future modal modes like helix or kakoune would plug in.
tour.languageLesson: VimFSA is a finite state machine that accumulates a pending command — count, operator, and motion (as in `2dw`) — across multiple keystrokes before producing an editor event. Modeling modal editing as an explicit FSA, separate from the keymap matcher, is what makes the scheme swappable: a different mode supplies a different state machine over the same editor event surface.

tour.title: Vim Motions, Text Objects & Wiring
tour.description: This final step fills in the modal engine's building blocks and closes the loop. find_char.rs implements f/F/t/T on-line search, word_iterator.rs yields word boundaries for w/b/e motions, matching_brackets.rs finds bracket pairs, text_objects/mod.rs aggregates the word/paragraph/quote/block text objects, and register.rs defines register-name validation and the black-hole register. Standing back: raw events (Step 4) are resolved by the keymap matcher (Step 6) into actions, a modal FSA (Step 12) interprets them using these primitives, and they mutate the buffer (Steps 9-10) which the render pipeline (Step 11) paints. A new pluggable modal mode would reuse these motion primitives and editor events while registering its own bindings and FSA through the keymap engine.
